region: Server text messages (cat 0x64 persistent box, cat 0x1f 2s toast) + error render states (renderTable indexed by NET+0x9c; states 1=cannot-connect, 2=connection-terminated)
summary:
## Response-body model for cat 0x64 / cat 0x1f + error render states

All addresses are FILE OFFSETS (guest = fo + 0x100000). The "NET" struct = `*(0x14ad10()) + 0xa3ac`. Key NET fields:
- `NET+0xa0` = 256-byte EUC-KR message buffer (the text shown to the user).
- `NET+0x9c` = u32 **dialog render-state** (indexes renderTable).
- `NET+0x460` = u8 icon flag, `NET+0x461` = u8 "message present/show" flag.

### renderTable (static @ fo 0xb32ec, pointer word @ sl+0x6a8=fo 0xb32e8, dispatched at fo 0x5aef4 by `NET[0x9c]`)
| idx | fn fo | meaning | draws |
|----|-------|---------|-------|
| 0 | 0x7285c | idle | no-op (returns) |
| 1 | 0x7286c | **CANNOT CONNECT** | fixed str 0xaa800; on give-up pops it as 2s toast |
| 2 | 0x729d4 | **CONNECTION TERMINATED** | fixed str 0xaa830 + "확인" button (0xaa850) |
| 3 | 0x72b18 | generic msg box | `NET+0xa0` |
| 4 | 0x72cbc | cat64 op0 box | `NET+0xa0` |
| 5 | 0x72d64 | cat64 op1 box | `NET+0xa0` |
| 6 | 0x72e0c | cat64 op2 box | `NET+0xa0` |
| 7 | 0x72eb4 | cat1f toast (2s auto-dismiss) | `NET+0xa0` |
| 8-11 | 0x72fe8.. | other in-game UI | menus |

### (1) Server text message carriers
**cat 0x64** (handler fo 0x581a8) — PERSISTENT message box. Wire body is length-prefixed:
`[u32 total_len][0x64][op u8][msglen u8][msglen EUC-KR bytes]`. Client does `memcpy(NET+0xa0, payload+3, msglen)` @0x58218, NUL-terminates, then op-switch sets state: op0→`NET[0x9c]=4`, op1→5, op2→6 (+`0x17e4c4(0)`); op≥3 = text copied but no state change. Sets `NET[0x461]=1`.

**cat 0x1f** (inline handler fo 0x56bb0) — 2-SECOND TOAST. Wire body: `[u32 total_len][0x1f][op(IGNORED)][reserved(IGNORED)][EUC-KR C-string \0]`. Handler calls `0x17e4c4(0)` then `showMessage(payload+3, 7, 1, 1)` @0x56bd4. showMessage (fn 0x175b98): `memset(NET+0xa0,0,0x100)`, `sprintf(NET+0xa0,"%s",payload+3)` @0x75c28, `NET[0x460]=1`, `NET[0x9c]=7`, `NET[0x461]=1`, and (timer arg=1) sets dismiss-timer `sl+0x9ac = now+2000ms`. renderTable[7] auto-calls `clearMessage(0)` when `now>=timer`.

A private server can push any Korean status/error string to the user with either cat (0x1f for a transient toast, 0x64 for a box that stays up).

### (2) Error render states — what triggers them
- **state 1 "서버와 접속할 수 없습니다..." (cannot connect)** is set when the WIPI socket callback reports **status code -5** (connect failed/refused/reset). Net-event handlers fn 0x74268 & 0x74388: `-5 → NET[0x9c]=1` @0x74338 / `clearMessage(1)` @0x744d2. Status -3/-4 = silent progress, -16(0x10) = silent close.
- **state 2 "서버와 연결이 종료되었습니다." (connection terminated)** — **exhaustive full-binary scan of every write to NET+0x9c shows values only {0,1,3,4,5,6,7,9,10,11,12,13,14}; NOTHING ever writes 2.** render[2] is **vestigial/unreachable** in this client build.

**Server guidance:** accept the TCP connection and keep it open (never RST/refuse) so the WIPI connect/read callback never returns -5 → the "cannot connect" screen (state 1) is avoided. The "connection terminated" screen (state 2) cannot be reached by any client code path, so it is not a concern. A mid-session server-side close surfaces as -5/-16 (→ "cannot connect" toast or silent), NOT the terminated screen.

Note: these two text handlers read the body by DIRECT offset (M+0xa len, M+0xb string) — they do NOT use the message read-cursor helper (that cursor is for login/warehouse cats).

reply_formats.layout: payload[0]=0x64 (cat, u8); payload[1]=op (u8: 0->render state4, 1->state5, 2->state6+call 0x17e4c4, >=3->text copied but NO state change); payload[2]=msglen (u8, count of text bytes); payload[3..3+msglen-1]=EUC-KR text (NO trailing NUL needed). Frame prefixed by [u32 LE total_len incl 4B header]. Little-endian header, single-byte fields for op/len.
reply_formats.effect: memcpy(NET+0xa0, payload+3, msglen) @fo0x58218; client NUL-terminates at NET+0xa0+msglen; sets NET+0x9c=4/5/6, NET+0x461=1. Rendered white by renderTable[4/5/6] (draw NET+0xa0). Persistent box (no auto-timer) - stays until dismissed by user input.

reply_formats.layout: payload[0]=0x1f (cat, u8); payload[1]=op -> IGNORED by handler; payload[2]=reserved -> IGNORED (never read); payload[3..]=NUL-terminated EUC-KR C-string (read via sprintf "%s"). String MUST start at payload[3]. Frame prefixed by [u32 LE total_len].
reply_formats.effect: handler 0x56bb0 -> 0x17e4c4(0) then showMessage(payload+3,7,1,1) @fo0x56bd4. showMessage(0x175b98): memset(NET+0xa0,0,256); sprintf(NET+0xa0,"%s",payload+3) @fo0x75c28; NET+0x460=1; NET+0x9c=7; NET+0x40=0; NET+0x461=1; dismiss timer sl+0x9ac=now+2000ms. renderTable[7] (0x72eb4) draws NET+0xa0 then clearMessage(0) once now>=timer -> disappears after ~2s.

reply_formats.cat_op: error render state 1 (no server reply; driven by socket status -5)
reply_formats.layout: No wire body. NET+0x9c(u32)=1 set by net-event handlers fn 0x74268/0x74388 when WIPI socket callback status == -5 (movs r3,#1; str [r2+0x9c] @fo0x74338; also clearMessage(1) @fo0x744d2).
reply_formats.effect: renderTable[1]=fo 0x7286c draws fixed EUC-KR string @fo 0xaa800 = '서버와 접속할 수 없습니다. 잠시후 시도해주세요.' (Cannot connect to server). Server AVOIDS by accepting the connection (no RST/refuse) so status never becomes -5.

reply_formats.layout: No wire body and NO writer: full-binary scan found no code writing 2 to NET+0x9c. Would require NET+0x9c(u32)=2.
reply_formats.effect: renderTable[2]=fo 0x729d4 draws fixed str @fo 0xaa830 = '서버와 연결이 종료되었습니다.' (Connection terminated) + '@OK:}확인' button @fo 0xaa850. Dead code in this build - the server cannot accidentally trigger it.

claims.statement: cat 0x64 handler (fo 0x581a8) copies a length-prefixed EUC-KR string to NET+0xa0: dest=NET+0xa0, src=payload[3] (M+0xb), len=payload[2] (M+0xa), then NUL-terminates.
claims.evidence: fo 0x58200 'adds r1,#0xa0' (dest NET+0xa0); fo 0x5820a 'adds r2,#0xb' (src M+0xb=payload[3]); fo 0x581e4 'ldrb r3=[M+0xa]' (len=payload[2]); fo 0x58218 'bl #0x19f624' (memcpy); fo 0x58234 'strb #0,[NET+0xa0+len]' NUL-term.

claims.statement: cat 0x64 op sub-switch: op0->NET[0x9c]=4, op1->5, op2->6 (+0x17e4c4(0)), op>=3 -> text copied but no state change. NET[0x461]=1 in all handled cases.
claims.evidence: fo 0x5827e 'movs r3,#4; str [r2+0x9c]' (op0); fo 0x5829c '#5' (op1); fo 0x582c0 '#6' (op2) with fo 0x582b4 'movs r0,#0; bl 0x17e4c4'; branch logic fo 0x5824a cmp#1 / 0x58256 bgt / 0x58262 cmp#0; each case ends 'str #1,[NET+0x461]'.

claims.statement: cat 0x1f handler (fo 0x56bb0) ignores op (payload[1]) and payload[2]; the message is a NUL-terminated EUC-KR C-string starting at payload[3], rendered via showMessage as a 2-second toast (state 7).
claims.evidence: fo 0x56bca 'adds r3,#0xb' (payload[3]); fo 0x56bce..d2 'movs r1,#7; r2,#1; r3,#1'; fo 0x56bd4 'bl 0x175b98'. Format string sl+0x484 -> fo 0xa95f8 = '%s' (verbatim copy). Handler never reads M+0xa (payload[2]).

claims.statement: showMessage (fn 0x175b98) writes NET+0xa0 (sprintf %s), NET+0x460=arg2, NET+0x9c=arg1(=mode), NET+0x461=arg3; when arg3==1 it arms auto-dismiss timer sl+0x9ac = now+2000ms; renderTable[7] auto-calls clearMessage(0) at expiry.
claims.evidence: fo 0x75bf6 memset(NET+0xa0,0,0x100); fo 0x75c28 'bl 0x1a42a4' sprintf w/ fmt sl+0x484='%s'; fo 0x75c3e 'strb [NET+0x460]'; fo 0x75c50 'str [NET+0x9c]'; fo 0x75c6e 'strb [NET+0x461]'; fo 0x75c76 'cmp arg3,#1' -> fo 0x75c94 literal 0x7d0(2000)+now stored to sl+0x9ac. render7 fo 0x72fc8 'movs r0,#0; bl 0x175cdc' on timer expiry.

claims.statement: NET+0x9c is the dialog render-state index into the static renderTable at fo 0xb32ec (12 entries; pointer word sl+0x6a8 @ fo 0xb32e8 relocates to it). Dispatcher at fo 0x5aef4 reads NET[0x9c], <<2, indexes table, indirect-calls.
claims.evidence: fo 0x5aef4 'adds r3,#0x9c; ldr r3,[r3]; lsls r3,#2; adds r2,r3,r2; ldr r2,[r2]; bl 0x1a429c'. Static tbl[0..3] fns resolve to 0x7285c,0x7286c,0x729d4,0x72b18 (indices 0-3 exact). render[2] ptr found ONLY at fo 0xb32f4 (tbl idx2).

claims.statement: renderTable[1]=fo 0x7286c shows 'cannot connect' (fo 0xaa800); renderTable[2]=fo 0x729d4 shows 'connection terminated' (fo 0xaa830) + OK button (fo 0xaa850).
claims.evidence: render1 loads sl+0x994->fo 0xaa800 at fo 0x7299c and showMessage(...,7,1,1) fo 0x7299c-0x729aa. render2 loads sl+0x998->fo 0xaa830 at fo 0x72a56 -> 0x15aacc(white), and sl+0x99c->fo 0xaa850 button -> 0x13ecfc at fo 0x72aee. Strings decoded EUC-KR: 0xaa800='서버와 접속할 수 없습니다. 잠시후 시도해주세요.', 0xaa830='서버와 연결이 종료되었습니다.', 0xaa850='@OK:}확인'.

claims.statement: The 'cannot connect' error (state 1) is triggered by WIPI socket callback status code -5, NOT by a server response. Status -3/-4 = silent progress; -16 = silent close (clearMessage 0).
claims.evidence: net-event handlers fn 0x74268 & 0x74388: fo 0x7430c 'movs r1,#5; rsbs (=-5); cmp; bne' then fo 0x74338 'movs r3,#1; str [r2+0x9c]; bl 0x17e344'; second handler fo 0x744d0 'movs r0,#1; bl 0x175cdc(clearMessage 1)'. -3/-4 branch fo 0x742a8/0x742b6 sets only +0x98 flag; -16 branch fo 0x74508 -> clearMessage(0).

claims.statement: No code path ever sets NET+0x9c=2, so renderTable[2] 'connection terminated' is unreachable/vestigial in this client build.
claims.evidence: Full-binary decode of every 'adds rN,#0x9c' writer plus both state helpers: direct writers produce only {0,4,5,6,12,1}; setState/clearMessage(0x75cdc) callers pass r0 in {0,1,3}; showMessage(0x175b98) 58 callers pass mode(r1) in {3,5,7,9,10,11,13,14}. Value 2 appears in none. str [+0x9c] is a word write and 0x9c>0x7c forbids str-imm, so all writes must use the scanned 'adds #0x9c' form.

claims.statement: renderTable[0]=fo 0x7285c is a no-op (idle: no dialog). renderTable[4/5/6]=cat64 boxes and [3]=generic box all render the same NET+0xa0 buffer white via 0x15aacc, with an optional icon gated on NET+0x460.
claims.evidence: render0 fo 0x7285c: push/str r0/pop only (empty). render4 fo 0x72cbc: fo 0x72cf8 checks NET+0x460 for icon (0x10defc), fo 0x72d3c checks NET+0xa0!=0 then fo 0x72d58 '0x15aacc(NET+0xa0,0xff,0xff,0xff)'. Same pattern in render3/5/6/7.

claims.statement: To reach the client, both text-message handlers require the standard response frame [u32 LE total_len incl 4B header][cat][op][body]; cat 0x64 needs total_len consistent with 7+msglen and cat 0x1f needs a NUL byte terminating the string at payload[3..].
claims.evidence: Dispatcher model (M=*node+8; M[8]=cat=payload[0]; M[9]=op; M[0xa]=payload[2]). cat64 uses payload[2] as its own length so it is self-describing; cat1f relies on the sprintf '%s' NUL scan (fmt fo 0xa95f8).

claims.statement: 0x17e4c4(flag) (called by cat64 op2 and cat1f) clears UI latch flags *(sl+0x814)=0 and *(sl+0xa44)=0 and, when flag==0, stops an active timed channel (sets a 64-bit field at *(sl+0x9d0) to -1, clears its +0x8/+0xc/+0x14). Cosmetic side-effect of presenting a message; not part of the wire format.
claims.evidence: fo 0x7e4d8 'strb #0,[*(sl+0x814)]'; fo 0x7e4e2 'strb #0,[*(sl+0xa44)]'; fo 0x7e4e4 'cmp r0,#0; bne skip'; fo 0x7e504-0x7e510 store -1 / 0 into *(sl+0x9d0) struct.

claims.statement: Supplementary strings confirm the message system also drives warehouse/economy/cash-shop feedback (relevant to the private-server warehouse feature).
claims.evidence: sl+0x9b4->fo 0xaa8ac='삭제하였습니다.'(deleted); sl+0x9b8->fo 0xaa8bc='돈 내리기 중입니다.'(withdrawing money); sl+0x9bc->fo 0xaa8d0='캐시템 구입중입니다.;(강제 종료시 아이템이 사라질 수 있습니다.)'(buying cash item). sl+0x9b4 is shown via showMessage(mode7) in net-handler B -5 branch fo 0x744ca.

open_questions: Exact dismissal/next-screen semantics that distinguish cat64 op0 vs op1 vs op2 (render 4/5/6 all draw NET+0xa0 identically; the op difference likely lives in the input/key handler that consumes NET+0x461, not decoded here).
Whether any non-code (initial/garbage) path could leave NET+0x9c=2 at boot; NET appears zero-initialized (state 0 idle), so practically no, but the struct initializer was not disassembled.
Precise role of the second net-event handler (fo 0x74388) vs first (fo 0x74268) - likely login-socket vs warehouse/economy-socket callbacks; both map status -5 to the same 'cannot connect' outcome.
